Reference evapotranspiration fraction

Source: R/metric-et.R
ef_etrf.Rd

Computes the reference evapotranspiration fraction \(ETrF\) at the satellite overpass time: the ratio of the instantaneous actual evapotranspiration to the reference evapotranspiration at the same instant. In METRIC this fraction is assumed constant during the day and is used to extrapolate the instantaneous estimate to a daily value (see ef_et_daily()).

Usage

ef_etrf(et_inst, etr_inst, reference)

Arguments

et_inst

Numeric. Instantaneous evapotranspiration \(ET_{inst}\) [mm h-1], for example from ef_et_inst(). Any finite value; negative values are allowed and kept.

etr_inst

Numeric. Reference evapotranspiration at the same instant (the overpass time of each pixel) [mm h-1]. Must be finite and > 0.

reference

Character. The reference crop of etr_inst, with no default: "alfalfa" (tall reference, ETr) or "grass" (short reference, ETo). An ETrF is defined only with respect to one reference; see Details.

Value

A numeric vector of the reference evapotranspiration fraction \(ETrF\) [-] with the common length of the inputs. If the inputs include matrices or arrays (all with the same dim), the result keeps that dim. Values are returned unchanged, whatever their sign or magnitude.

Details

The fraction is $$ETrF = \frac{ET_{inst}}{ETr_{inst}}$$ where \(ET_{inst}\) is et_inst and \(ETr_{inst}\) is etr_inst, both in mm h-1 at the same instant.

Reference crop: an ETrF based on alfalfa is not comparable with one based on grass. etr_inst, the daily reference evapotranspiration used by ef_et_daily() and the boundary condition of the cold anchor pixel must all refer to the same reference crop; otherwise the daily estimate is wrong without any arithmetic error. reference does not change the computation: it makes the choice explicit. The consistency check between the steps is made by the orchestration layer.

The temporal basis of etr_inst (instantaneous rate or hourly reference ET of a period centred on the overpass time) is defined by the meteorological forcing and must be recorded in the provenance.

Negative values of et_inst give a negative ETrF, returned unchanged and without a warning. No plausible range of ETrF is checked or flagged: the upper limit has no verified reference yet. Values are never truncated.

Missing values (NA, NaN) in any input propagate to the corresponding output element, without errors or warnings. Arguments must be numeric (double or integer) and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled, arrays with a dim are not. A non-positive etr_inst (it would give an infinite or meaningless fraction) or any infinite value raises an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). A missing reference raises earthflux_missing_input; an unknown one, earthflux_input_error.

Verification status: CANDIDATA (corroborated by secondary sources, Olmedo et al., 2016, Eq. 4). It is implemented as an operational definition; its form and equation number in Allen et al. (2007) have not been verified.

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Olmedo, G. F., Ortega-Farias, S., de la Fuente-Saiz, D., Fonseca-Luengo, D., & Fuentes-Penailillo, F. (2016). water: Tools and functions to estimate actual evapotranspiration using land surface energy balance models in R. The R Journal, 8(2), 352-369. doi:10.32614/RJ-2016-051

See also

Other latent heat and evapotranspiration functions: ef_et_daily(), ef_et_inst(), ef_latent_heat()

Examples

# 0.72 mm h-1 against an alfalfa reference of 0.80 mm h-1: 0.9
ef_etrf(et_inst = 0.72, etr_inst = 0.80, reference = "alfalfa")
#> [1] 0.9

# Negative and high fractions are returned unchanged
ef_etrf(et_inst = c(-0.072, 0.9), etr_inst = c(0.80, 0.75),
        reference = "alfalfa")
#> [1] -0.09  1.20
